query: edge AI face recognition for access control: anti-spoofing techniques, on-device inference hardware, and commercial market landscape 2026

facts.desc: ISO/IEC 30107-3:2023 (Edition 2) is the standard for biometric presentation attack detection Part 3: Testing and reporting. https://www.iso.org/standard/79520.html
APCER/BPCER are the standardized PAD error metrics reported under ISO/IEC 30107-3. https://www.iso.org/standard/79520.html

NIST's FRVT was split/rebranded into FRTE (Face Recognition Technology Evaluation) and FATE; it is the reference accuracy benchmark for face recognition algorithms. https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/face-technology-evaluations-frtefate
NIST's FATE PAD track published NISTIR 8491 (Sept 2023) evaluating 82 passive software-based face PAD algorithms on conventional 2D imagery. https://pages.nist.gov/frvt/html/frvt_pad.html

Known presentation attack instruments include printed photos, screen/video replay, and 3D masks, per the ISO/IEC 30107 attack taxonomy used by NIST FATE PAD. https://pages.nist.gov/frvt/html/frvt_pad.html
Hailo-8 edge AI accelerator delivers up to 26 TOPS at ~2.5 W typical power with integrated on-chip memory. https://hailo.ai/products/ai-accelerators/hailo-8-ai-accelerator/
NVIDIA Jetson Orin family spans up to 275 TOPS (AGX Orin); Orin Nano up to 67 TOPS — per NVIDIA's official spec table. https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/autonomous-machines/embedded-systems/jetson-orin/

Access control is the largest application segment of the facial recognition market (~36% of 2025 revenue per Grand View Research). https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/facial-recognition-market

traps.desc: Wrong part number: Part 1 is the framework; PAD testing/reporting and APCER/BPCER are defined in Part 3 (ISO/IEC 30107-3:2023). https://www.iso.org/standard/79520.html
Marketing falsehood: NIST FRTE/FATE evaluates and benchmarks algorithms but does not certify or approve products. https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/face-technology-evaluations-frtefate
Wrong magnitude: Hailo-8 is 26 TOPS, not hundreds of TOPS (confusion with datacenter-class accelerators). https://hailo.ai/products/ai-accelerators/hailo-8-ai-accelerator/
Spec mix-up: Jetson Orin Nano tops out at 67 TOPS; 275 TOPS is AGX Orin, 157 TOPS is Orin NX. https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/autonomous-machines/embedded-systems/jetson-orin/
False absolutism: no PAD/liveness mechanism is 100% spoof-proof — NIST IR 8491 found varied, imperfect performance across 82 passive PAD algorithms. https://pages.nist.gov/frvt/html/frvt_pad.html

contested.desc: Grand View Research: USD 8.5B in 2026 (https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/facial-recognition-market) vs Mordor Intelligence USD 9.95B (https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/facial-recognition-market) and MarketsandMarkets USD 10.02B in 2026 (https://www.marketsandmarkets.com/Market-Reports/facial-recognition-market-995.html).

Active challenge-response liveness (blink/turn-head) vs passive no-gesture liveness; iProov argues passive is more usable and harder to reverse-engineer (https://www.iproov.com/blog/passive-authentication-for-online-identity), while active challenge-response remains widely deployed.

Hardware depth/IR sensing is favored for high-security deployments (3D held ~38% technology share in 2025 per Grand View Research) vs passive software-based PAD on 2D imagery — the class NIST IR 8491 evaluated (https://pages.nist.gov/frvt/html/frvt_pad.html).
